newsitem.title: SPAIN: Popular shares up 6 pct on news of buyback.
newsitem.headline: Popular shares up 6 pct on news of buyback.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Banco Popular soared over six percent on Wednesday after it said it was buying back 35 billion pesetas' worth of stock, which would then be cancelled.
Popular also said it would split stock four for one, with the face value falling to 125 pesetas from 500 pesetas.
At 1430 GMT, Popular was up 1,800 pesetas, or 6.68 percent, to 28,750 pesetas while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares rose 1.17 percent to 5,796.88.

"This gives the shares a boost in terms of liquidity. Stocks that have been split before now have risen up to 15 percent because you have to add back the illiquidity premium the market was paying before," said a dealer at Central Hispano Bolsa.
"You're basically facilitating the operations of smaller scale investors in the market."
But how much of the shares the bank had already bought would be key, the dealer added.
"Judging from what the market's doing it looks like most people think they haven't bought any yet," the dealer added.
Popular also announced first quarter net attributable profit of 16.14 billion pesetas versus 14.45 billion pesetas in the same period a year-earlier.
